q: 1. The difference in the lengths of an arc and its subtended chord on the earth surface for a distance of 18.2 km, is only
explain: The arc-to-chord correction is given by d3/(24R2); for a distance of about 18.2 km on the earth's surface (R ~ 6370 km) this works out to approximately 10 mm, which is why curvature is ignored for ordinary plane surveys of this extent.

q: 2. The least count of a vernier scale is
options: sum of the smallest division of main and vernier scales
value of one division of the primary scale divided by total number of division of vernier scale
value of one division of vernire scale divided by total number of division of primary scale
explain: Least count of a vernier = (value of one main scale division) / (total number of divisions on the vernier scale); this is the smallest reading directly obtainable with the vernier.

q: 3. The method of measuring distance by pacing is chiefly used in
explain: Pacing gives only approximate distances and is used mainly during reconnaissance surveys, where a quick rough idea of the terrain and distances is needed before detailed survey work.

q: 4. The object of surveying is to be prepare
explain: The fundamental purpose of any survey is to determine the relative positions of points so that a map or plan of the area can be prepared.

q: 5. A plumb line is
options: a line parallel to vertical line
a line perpendicular to level line
a line perpendicular to horizontal line
explain: A plumb line is the vertical line indicated by a suspended plumb bob, which is perpendicular to every level (horizontal) line at that point.

q: 6. While surveying a plot of land by plane tabling, the field observations
options: and plotting do not proceed simultaneously
and recorded in field books to be plotted later
explain: Plane tabling is unique among surveying methods in that field observation and plotting happen simultaneously on the table sheet in the field itself, eliminating the need for a separate field book.

q: 7. A plain scale is used to read
explain: A plain scale has only primary and secondary divisions, allowing two dimensions (e.g., units and tenths, such as metres and decimetres) to be read directly.

q: 8. Survey plotting can be done with an accuracy of
explain: With good drafting instruments and practice, survey plotting can typically achieve an accuracy of about 0.25 mm on the plotted sheet.

q: 9. The angle between two plane mirrors of optical square, is
explain: An optical square uses two mirrors inclined at 45 deg to each other, which by the double-reflection principle deviates a ray of light through 90 deg, enabling right angles to be set out.

q: 10. A clinometer is used for
explain: A clinometer is a simple instrument used to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground.

q: 11. For the construction of highway
options: both longitudinal and cross sections are required
explain: Highway design and earthwork computation require both longitudinal sections (to fix the vertical alignment/gradient) and cross-sections (to compute cut and fill quantities).

q: 12. Pantagraph is used for
explain: A pantograph is a mechanical linkage instrument used to copy, enlarge, or reduce plans and drawings to a different scale.

q: 13. While surveying a plot of land by Plane tabling, the field observations
options: and plotting do not proceed simultaneously
and recorded in field books to be plotted later
explain: The key characteristic of plane table surveying is that field observation and plotting are done together at the same time in the field, unlike other methods where plotting is done later in the office.

q: 14. The branch of surveying in which both horizontal and vertical positions of a point, are determined by making instrumental observations, is known
explain: As per the book's answer key, this branch is designated 'tachemetry' (an alternate spelling of tacheometry), the surveying method that determines both horizontal and vertical positions instrumentally without chaining.

q: 15. The systematic errors which persist and have regular effects in the performance of a survey operation are due to
explain: Systematic errors that follow a definite, regular pattern typically arise from faulty or improperly adjusted instruments, rather than random human lapses.

q: 16. Pick up the method of surveying in which field observations and plotting proceed simultaneously from the following
explain: Plane table surveying is unique in that field observation and plotting are carried out together at the same time in the field.

q: 17. Theory of probability is applied to
explain: The theory of probability is applied specifically to accidental (random) errors, since these follow the laws of chance, unlike systematic/cumulative errors which have a definite known cause and sign.

q: 18. Geodetic survey is different from plane surveying because of
options: the curvature of the earth is considered
explain: The key distinguishing feature of geodetic surveying from plane surveying is that the curvature of the earth is taken into account in geodetic computations.

q: 19. In case of geographical maps, the scale is usually
explain: Geographical maps, which cover very large regions such as countries or continents, typically use small scales in the range of about 1 cm representing 5 km up to 160 km.

q: 20. The representative fraction of the scale 1cm = 1 kilometer will be
explain: 1 cm = 1 km = 100,000 cm, so the representative fraction is 1/1,00,000 (i.e., 1/10,00,00 in the Indian numbering format given).

q: 21. Cadastral map is a map having
explain: Cadastral maps, which show detailed property boundaries, are drawn to a large scale for adequate accuracy and clarity of individual plots.

q: 22. The maximum allowable limit up to that a measurement may vary from the true value is known as
explain: The permissible error is defined as the maximum allowable deviation of a measured value from its true value, within the specified precision of the survey.

q: 23. Geodetic surveying is different from plane surveying because of
options: the large difference of elevations between various points
explain: Geodetic surveying differs fundamentally from plane surveying because it covers very large areas where the curvature of the earth cannot be ignored, requiring spherical (geodetic) rather than plane computations.

q: 24. The principle of optics used in the construction of an optical square is
explain: An optical square works on the principle of double reflection, using two mirrors inclined at 45 deg to each other to deviate a ray of light through exactly 90 deg.

q: 25. When 1 cm on a map represents 10 m on the ground, the representative fraction of the scale is
explain: 1 cm = 10 m = 1000 cm, so the representative fraction is 1:1000, i.e., 1/1000.

q: 26. The representative fraction 1/2500 means that the scale is
explain: RF of 1/2500 means 1 cm on the map represents 2500 cm on the ground, which equals 25 m.

q: 27. Cross hairs in surveying telescope are fitted
options: at the centre of the telescope
in the optical center of the eye-piece
explain: Cross hairs are mounted on a diaphragm located in front of the eyepiece at the focal plane of the objective.

q: 28. The difference between the most probable value and its observed value is
explain: The residual error (or residual) is defined as the difference between the most probable value (usually the mean of observations) and any individual observed value.

q: 29. Mistakes which may produce a very serious effect upon the final results arise due to
explain: Serious mistakes in survey work generally result from a combination of human factors - inattention, inexperience, and carelessness - so all of these are valid causes.

q: 30. The working from whole to the part is done in surveying in order to ensure that
options: survey work is completed more quickly
errors and mistakes of one portion do not affect the remaining portion
explain: Working from whole to part localizes errors, so that any small error made in one part of the survey does not propagate and magnify across the rest of the survey area.

q: 31. The systematic errors which persist and have regular effects in the performance of a survey operations, are due to
explain: Systematic errors, which follow a definite mathematical/physical law and persist consistently, typically arise from a faulty (mis-calibrated or maladjusted) instrument.

q: 32. When 1 cm on a map represents 10m on the ground, the representative fraction of the scale in
explain: 1 cm represents 10 m = 1000 cm, so the representative fraction is 1/1000.

q: 33. The method of reversal
options: is usually directed to examine whether a certain part is truly parallel or perpendicular to another
makes the erroneous relationship between parts evident
explain: The method of reversal serves both purposes - it examines whether parts of an instrument are truly parallel/perpendicular to each other, and in doing so makes any erroneous relationship between them evident.

q: 34. The apparent error on reversal is
explain: When an instrumental error is examined by the method of reversal, the apparent (observed) error is exactly twice the actual error present in the instrument's adjustment.

q: 35. The method of surveying used for determining the relative height of points on the surface of the earth is called
explain: Differential levelling is the method specifically used to determine the relative heights (difference in elevation) of points on the earth's surface.

q: 36. A branch of surveying in which the horizontal and vertical distances of points are obtained by instrumental observations, is known as
explain: Tacheometric surveying is defined as the branch in which both horizontal and vertical distances are obtained rapidly through instrumental (stadia) observations, without chaining.

q: 37. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: In levelling, the effect of curvature is to decrease the staff reading.
The effect of refraction in levelling is to increase the staff reading.
The combined effect of curvature and refraction in levelling is to increase the staff reading.
explain: Actually curvature increases the apparent staff reading (makes points look lower), refraction (partially) decreases it, but per the answer key given, the combined net effect statement along with the other individual statements is taken as correct overall, hence option (d), all of the above, is marked correct in this text.

q: 38. The types of survey used for Geodetic survey is
explain: Geodetic surveys cover large areas and require extreme accuracy to account for earth's curvature, necessitating precise leveling methods.

q: 39. The angle between two plane mirrors of the optical square is kept
explain: The two plane mirrors of an optical square are set at exactly 45 degrees to each other to achieve the required 90-degree deflection of the sight line.

q: 40. The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously, is called
explain: As established, plane table surveying is the unique method where field observation and plotting proceed together, simultaneously.

q: 41. The type of surveying which requires least office work is
explain: Since plotting is done directly in the field alongside observation in plane table surveying, it requires the least amount of subsequent office (indoor) computation and plotting work.

q: 42. In order to determine the natural features such as valley, rivers, lakes etc., the surveying prepared is
explain: As in Q201, topographical surveying is used to determine and depict natural features such as valleys, rivers, and lakes.

q: 43. Which of the following can fulfill the objective of the airport survey?
explain: An airport survey requires detailed information on the characteristics of the soil, which is essential for pavement/runway design and foundation planning.

q: 44. Grid lines are parallel to
options: magnetic meridian of the central point of the grid
line representing the central true meridian of the grid
explain: In a survey grid system, all grid lines running north-south are drawn parallel to the line representing the central true meridian of the grid zone.

q: 45. The sum of the interior angles of a geometrical figure laid on the surface of the earth differs from that of the corresponding plane figure only to the extent of one second for every
explain: Due to the earth's curvature, the spherical excess in the interior angles of a figure on the earth's surface amounts to about one second of arc for every 100 sq. km of area (in this text's convention).

q: 46. Diaphragm of a surveying telescope is held inside
options: telescope at the end nearer the eye-piece
explain: The diaphragm (cross-hair ring) is mounted inside the telescope tube, positioned roughly at its mid-point between the objective and the eyepiece.

q: 47. In order to determine the natural features such as valleys, rivers, lakes, etc., the surveying preferred is
explain: Topographical surveying is specifically carried out to determine and depict natural features of the terrain such as valleys, rivers, and lakes, along with artificial features.

q: 48. The surveying used to determine additional details such as boundaries of fields, is called
explain: Cadastral surveying is specifically carried out to determine property boundaries, such as those of individual fields, for revenue and legal purposes.

q: 49. The fundamental principle of surveying is to work from the
explain: The fundamental principle of all surveying is to work from the whole to the part, establishing a rough, accurate framework first before adding progressively finer detail within it.

q: 50. The working from whole to the part is done in surveying in order to ensure that
options: surveying work is completed more quickly
errors and mistakes of one portion do not affected the remaining portion
explain: Working from whole to part localizes errors - if a mistake occurs in a minor detail survey, it does not affect the accuracy of the main framework or other parts of the survey.
